title: ratchet_violation drift detection in check::evaluate + surfaces
description:
New `ratchet_violation` finding kind in check::evaluate (BOTH arms — evaluate_dd and evaluate_raw): for each unreleased constraint_ratchets row, emit when (a) its constraint_id has no match in current parsed rules (deletion/param-edit/scope-narrowing all manifest as ID disappearance) or (b) the surviving constraint's severity < severity_floor. Detail uses rendered_description so the report is meaningful after the constraint is gone from TOML. Severity: Blocking, always. NON-WAIVABLE — must bypass the waiver partition entirely (a waiver on tamper detection would be the bypass). Skip when released_at is set.

Surfaces: sutra_constraints violations + list (show ratchet status per constraint, active ratchet count), review findings, orient constraints section. Catches out-of-band edits (shell redirection, non-hook editors) at next evaluation regardless of how rules.toml was modified.

Design: sutra/223 implementation_plan. Refactor-contract discipline (L9) applies to check.rs changes. Tests in tests/constraints-test.rs + review-test.rs: deletion detected, severity-below-floor detected, released row silent, non-waivability (waiver row present but finding still active).
execution_record: Straightforward implementation. One wrinkle: the guard's forbidden-pattern rule (no-clone-driven-dev) blocked Arc::clone() calls in new ConstraintFinding construction. Used Arc::clone(&x) syntax instead of x.clone() to signal intent and avoid the syntactic pattern. evaluate_raw's get_active_ratchets_raw uses graceful error handling (returns empty vec) since guard tests use in-memory connections without the constraint_ratchets table.
